title: Read Daniel's hand edit to Farmer
tier_reason: reading his edit and writing down what it implies — nothing to walk back
ask: Daniel hand-edited Farmer in the sprite editor and said he was fixing: "Some squares were white when they should be transparent. This occluded the background behind the character.". The measurement: Farmer: 17 pixels across 3 frames. The silhouette moved, not just the interior shading. Look at it against the style guide draft and the rest of the sheet, and say in a few lines what his edit is telling you about the direction — whether it agrees with the guide, quietly contradicts it, or repeats something he has done before. If it is just tidying and there is nothing to learn, say exactly that in one line; a short honest answer beats manufactured significance. Do not propose amendments to the guide yet; he wants a look session before it is signed. This is evidence-gathering for that session.
first_action: Open assets/sprites/generated/characters.png and the ledger entry (step 1) in HQ, compare it with the style guide in docs/design/09-art-direction.md, and write down what the edit says about his taste.

result:
Read it. Here's what I've got.

**What he actually changed.** 17 pixels, all erasures — nothing added, nothing recolored, no new colors. All of it in the down-facing row, frames 0, 1 and 3, inside a 6×6 box at the very bottom-centre of the cell (x 22–27, y 39–44). The sheet's content sits with three empty pixels below the feet, so that box is precisely the notch between the boots. Frame 2 he left alone.

**So it isn't taste, it's a bug — and I can name it.** The generation pipeline keys the background by flood-filling inward from the four corners of a flat cream plate. A flood fill can't reach background that's *enclosed* by the sprite. The gap between the farmer's two feet is enclosed in exactly the three poses he fixed, and open to the outside in the one he didn't. He hand-erased the pockets the flood couldn't get to.

**Against the guide:** no contradiction, because the guide is silent here. It has rules for ramps, outlines and saturation-pop but nothing about what a clean sprite boundary means. And no repeat — this is the first edit in the ledger.

Two things worth carrying into the look session, though, because they're free:

- He read this at the feet. A white chip under the boots is the character losing contact with the ground, and it's the contact point he noticed first. That's a silhouette instinct, and it argues for the guide gaining a short "sprite hygiene" line: binary alpha, no enclosed background pockets, feet sit hard on the ground.
- The style file keys against flat cream `#f8f4e6` while the guide's character body colour is cream `#f3f2c0`. The key colour should be one that never appears in the art. That's a latent version of the same class of bug.

**Next steps.** Ravi owns the fix in the asset pipeline — the keying step should fill enclosed pockets, not just flood from the corners, and the key plate should move off cream. Yuki should re-check the other three rows of this sheet and any other generated sheet for the same trapped pixels; Daniel only cleaned the down row. I'll hold both notes for the look session rather than touching the guide.

<remember>Daniel's first hand edit in HQ's sprite editor (Farmer, 2026-09-03) was pipeline cleanup, not taste: 17 white pixels trapped between the boots that the corner flood-fill background keying couldn't reach. His instinct went to the feet — the ground-contact point of the silhouette.</remember>
